records.targetText: Actual PBPS harmonic flow and conserved weighted energyFan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang, arXiv:2609.06905v1, Algorithm1, Section3 and AppendixA.1. ASTIS completes the deterministic explicit-flow/weighted-energy details; stochastic Proposition3.1 is a separate consumer, not a theorem proved here.arXiv2609.06905v1/Lean4.33.0/Mathlibdb584cd6d46c92f209a44c0f1c829460d327499d · PBPS Algorithm1 harmonic arcs, Section3 exact dynamics and AppendixA.1 ODE/weighted-energy formulas; deterministic construction prerequisite for Proposition3.1 · faithful paraphraseComplete source statement (Samplinglib restatement)Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, including rank zero. Let V:E→ℝ be C² on all E, let α,β≥0 satisfy 0<α≤β and α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖² for all x

records.label: unit0-proof-1
records.targetText:
1. Establish the scale and joint continuitySince η>0, r=√η is positive, nonzero and r²=η. The canonical ASTIS gradient-continuity theorem applies to V∈C² after lowering its differentiability order to one. Hence c depends continuously on (y,xRef), and the displayed trigonometric and scalar operations make Φ jointly continuous in all four inputs. Joint Borel measurability follows for the actual product Borel spaces; it is used when reassembling the conclusions.r=η>0,r2=η,c(y,xref)=y−η∇V(xref) is continuous.Corresponding Lean step  have hr : 0 < Real.sqrt η := Real.sqrt_pos.2 hη
  have hr0 : Real.sqrt η ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hr
  have hr2 : (Real.sqrt η) ^ 2 = η := Real.sq_sqrt hη.le
  have hgrad : Continuous (fun x : E => gradient V x) :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.Calculus.Gr

records.label: unit0-proof-2
records.targetText:
2. Verify identity, group composition and inverseAt time zero the sine vanishes and cosine is one. Expanding Φ_s(Φ_tz), the cosine and sine addition formulas identify both coordinates with Φ_{s+t}z; division is legitimate because √η≠0. Taking s=−t or t=−s yields both inverse identities. All times are real, with no domain restriction.cos⁡(s+t)=cos⁡scos⁡t−sin⁡ssin⁡t,sin⁡(s+t)=sin⁡scos⁡t+cos⁡ssin⁡t,Φ−tΦt=ΦtΦ−t=id.Corresponding Lean step  have hzero (y xRef : E) (z : E × E) : Φ y xRef 0 z = z := by
    apply Prod.ext <;> dsimp [Φ]
    · simp only [Real.cos_zero, Real.sin_zero, one_smul, mul_zero, zero_smul, add_zero]
      module
    · simp
  have hgroup (y xRef : E) (s t : ℝ) (z : E × E) :
      Φ y xRef (s + t) z = Φ y xRef s (Φ y xRef t z) := by
    apply Prod.ext <;> dsimp [Φ]
    all_goal

records.label: unit0-proof-3
records.targetText:
3. Differentiate the two actual coordinatesDifferentiate the sine and cosine expressions while fixing y,xRef and the initial state. The position derivative is −sin(t)(x−c)+r cos(t)p=rP_t. For momentum, −cos(t)(x−c)/r−sin(t)p equals −(X_t−y)/r−r∇V(xRef), using c=y−η∇V(xRef) and r²=η. HasDerivAt.congr_deriv changes only the vector derivative expression; it supplies no ODE hypothesis.X˙t=−sin⁡t(x−c)+rcos⁡tp=rPt,P˙t=−cos⁡tr(x−c)−sin⁡tp=−Xt−yr−r∇V(xref).Corresponding Lean step  have hode (y xRef : E) (t : ℝ) (z : E × E) :
      HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => (Φ y xRef s z).1)
        (Real.sqrt η • (Φ y xRef t z).2) t ∧
      HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => (Φ y xRef s z).2)
        (-(Real.sqrt η)⁻¹ • ((Φ y xRef t z).1 - y) -
          Real.sqrt η • gradient V xRef) t := by
    constructor
    · have hx :=

records.label: unit0-proof-4
records.targetText:
4. Keep the weighted energy nonnegativeBoth squared norms are nonnegative. Since η>0, its inverse is nonnegative, and dividing their weighted sum by two preserves nonnegativity. Zero initial energy is included.H(z)=12(η−1‖x−c‖2+‖p‖2)≥0.Corresponding Lean step  have hnonneg (y xRef : E) (z : E × E) : 0 ≤ H y xRef z := by
    exact div_nonneg (add_nonneg (mul_nonneg (inv_nonneg.2 hη.le) (sq_nonneg _))
      (sq_nonneg _)) (by norm_num)

records.label: unit0-proof-5
records.targetText:
5. Cancel the mixed terms in the conserved energyPut q=x−c, C=cos t and S=sin t. Translate the first coordinate back by c and expand each individual squared norm. The mixed terms are +2CS⟨q,p⟩/r and −2CS⟨q,p⟩/r, which cancel. The remaining sum is (C²+S²)(r⁻²‖q‖²+‖p‖²). Using C²+S²=1 and r²=η gives H(Φ_tz)=H(z), with the exact factor one half retained.r−2‖Cq+rSp‖2+‖−Sq/r+Cp‖2=(C2+S2)(r−2‖q‖2+‖p‖2)=r−2‖q‖2+‖p‖2.Corresponding Lean step  have henergy (y xRef : E) (t : ℝ) (z : E × E) :
      H y xRef (Φ y xRef t z) = H y xRef z := by
    have hcenter : (Φ y xRef t z).1 - c y xRef =
        Real.cos t • (z.1 - c y xRef) + (Real.sqrt η * Real.sin t) • z.2 := by
      dsimp [Φ]
      module
    dsimp only [H]
    rw [hcenter]
    dsimp only [Φ]
    congr 1
    rw [norm_add_sq_real, norm_add_sq_rea

records.label: unit0-proof-6
records.targetText:
6. Evaluate the half-turn and collect the nine lawsAt t=π, sin π=0 and cos π=−1, so X_π=c−(x−c)=2c−x and P_π=−p. Collect the continuity/Borel, initial, group, two inverse, ODE, nonnegative-energy, conservation and half-turn conclusions. This endpoint belongs to a deterministic arc only; stochastic bounces may change the eventual terminal law.Φπ(x,p)=(c−(x−c),−p)=(2c−x,−p).Corresponding Lean step  have hpi (y xRef : E) (z : E × E) :
      Φ y xRef Real.pi z = ((2 : ℝ) • c y xRef - z.1, -z.2) := by
    apply Prod.ext <;> dsimp [Φ]
    · simp only [Real.cos_pi, Real.sin_pi, mul_zero, zero_smul, add_zero, neg_smul,
        one_smul]
      module
    · simp
  exact ⟨hcont, hcont.measurable, hzero, hgroup, hinverse, hode, hnonneg, henergy, hpi⟩
